messages:
Maya Patel: quick handoff note — I'm primary for 18:00-02:00 UTC. Sam is out 00:30-01:00 UTC so there is a short coverage gap; Priya will be secondary escalation during that window. If pager hits during gap, follow escalation matrix below.

Sam Lee: can be on phone 00:15-00:45 if something critical comes up, but won't be able to respond in slack until ~01:10. sorry for the tight window.

Maya Patel: thanks. two practical things: 1) if you see P1/P1-like customer impact (>=2 regions or significant traffic loss), page Priya immediately and start bridge. 2) for P2 latency spikes, triage in channel first and only page on-call phone if >15min or customer-facing errors.

Priya Raman: confirmed I'll be reachable on call during 00:30-01:30 UTC for any escalations. If something needs exec-level attention, page Alex and then Jordan (they're on rotation for exec notify).

Maya Patel: runbook pointers — primary runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency (shortlink). If you need quick diagnostics:
```
rdwctl tail inference-prod --since 10m | grep "tail_latency" -A3
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/serving-router --tail=200 | grep ERROR
```
If you hit KV-cache thrash, try toggling the prefix cache per instructions in the runbook.

Jordan Kim: adding quick escalation phone chain so it's explicit:
- Pager -> Primary on-call
- If no ack in 5m or severity escalates -> Page Priya Raman (SRE Lead)
- If P1 or customer impact -> Page Alex Torres (Support Director) AND start bridge + notify execs (Jordan/K8 rotation)
- If paging fails -> ops-bot escalate to on-call cell phone and send SMS: /ops escalate-phone

Alex Torres: note on customer impact thresholds: use these heuristics —
- P1: outage or >20% error rate for 5+ min across 2+ regions
- P2: latency >3x p50 and impacting important customers (from support flags)
- P3: isolated degradation, no immediate paging.
If you're uncertain, page Priya and she'll triage.

incident-bot: [ALERT] inference-prod: tail-latency spike detected (source=prometheus, alert_id=ALRT-9832). severity=suspected-P2. fired_at=6212345688. PagerDuty incident created: PD-4921.

Maya Patel: received the alert. I'm starting the quick checklist from the runbook. Assigning: I'll check the serving-router logs; Sam (if reachable) can validate KV cache logs once back.

Sam Lee: ack via phone — I can run the KV cache check now, dialing in briefly.

Maya Patel: findings so far: serving-router shows a spike in tail latency correlated with a small spike of long context requests. Not seeing increased error 5xx yet.

Priya Raman: thanks — since it's a suspected-P2 and PD incident exists, start a quick bridge (no more than 15 min initial), invite support (Alex) and engineering (Jordan). If we see errors or customer-visible timeouts, escalate to P1.

Jordan Kim: starting bridge and posting link: https://meet.redwood/bridges/PD-4921. Also pinned the runbook.

Alex Torres: I'm on the bridge. flagging two customers on the watchlist — CustA and CustB; support tickets already opened.

Maya Patel: temporary mitigation attempt: reduced batching window on the router (applied via canary). Monitoring for 2 minutes.

ops-bot: run command accepted: `rdwctl set-config router.batch_window=20ms --canary`. Canary applied to 10% of routers.

Maya Patel: after canary: one router shows latency drop, overall tail improved slightly but still elevated. We'll continue canary and prepare to roll to 50% if stable.

Priya Raman: decision: continue canary for 10m; if no errors increase, roll to 50% and notify customers postmortem. If errors spike, rollback immediately and escalate to P1.

Sam Lee: will follow up with KV-cache logs when fully back online and post findings here.

Maya Patel: final note for handoff — after 02:00 UTC, primary rotates to Jordan. If anything persists beyond the window, make sure PD alerts have the correct owners. Leaving this thread pinned to the shift channel. :thumbsup:
